verses.text: When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he gathered the people of Judah and Benjamin, one hundred eighty thousand chosen soldiers, to fight against Israel and win the kingdom back for Rehoboam.
But the LORD's message came to Shemaiah, the man of God. He said,
"Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the Israelites in Judah and Benjamin. Say,
'The LORD says: Do not go up and fight against your brothers! Everyone go back home, because I made this happen.'" So they obeyed the LORD's words and did not go to attack Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built towns in Judah for defense.
He built up Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
Beth Zur, Soco, Adullam,
Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. These were strong, walled towns in Judah and Benjamin.
He made the forts strong and put commanders in them, with supplies of food, olive oil, and wine.
He put shields and spears in every town and made them very strong. So Judah and Benjamin belonged to him.
The priests and Levites from all over Israel came from their areas and stood with him.
The Levites left their pasture lands and their property and came to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons would not let them serve as priests of the LORD.
Jeroboam chose his own priests for the hilltop shrines and for the goat and calf idols he had made.
After the Levites, people from all the tribes of Israel who had set their hearts on seeking the LORD, the God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
They made the kingdom of Judah strong and supported Rehoboam son of Solomon for three years, because for three years they lived the way David and Solomon had lived.
Rehoboam married Mahalath. She was the daughter of Jerimoth son of David, and of Abihail, the daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
She had sons for him: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
After her, he married Maacah, Absalom's granddaughter. She had Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith for him.
Rehoboam loved Maacah, Absalom's granddaughter, more than all his other wives and slave wives. He had eighteen wives and sixty slave wives, and he had twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
Rehoboam made Abijah son of Maacah the chief leader among his brothers, because he planned to make him king.
He acted wisely and spread some of his sons through all the areas of Judah and Benjamin, to every walled town. He gave them plenty of food and found many wives for them.
